151: 
152: Add the following keys to the existing AgentState through narrow integration edits: course_run (RunContext), evidence_index, argument_index, verified_metrics, sentiment_assessment and publication_result. These are separate state keys; do not have parallel nodes overwrite an entire common nested dictionary. Existing nodes own their existing report strings. New owner records are not reconstructed from those strings. Avoid new dependencies or replacement of the orchestrator.
153: 
154: For sentiment, the analyst emits sentiment_assessment and renders its legacy sentiment_report from that same record, including the model-message/report views. At 0/3, the selected v1 path skips the sentiment model call and creates a deterministic missing-data narrative with UNKNOWN/null. With data, finalize the model assessment while preserving coverage; provider/free-text fallback cannot restore a made-up default score. The FR-03 task plan tests schema/renderer compatibility before selecting the internal Pydantic adaptation. FR-01 can publish from valid non-sentiment evidence when its own gate passes.

At the two NFR-02 sites use prepare_context; elsewhere use a nonreducing READY adapter so NFR-01 covers all sends without accidentally applying a 64 KiB cap to every call. All branches then use the same C4 dispatch boundary. Tests can use fixed fake producers/consumers until integration, but combined graph acceptance needs the real connected owner modules.

31: Context sizing/reduction (NFR-02) and publication gating (FR-01 / INV-01) are
32: owned elsewhere and are deliberately not implemented here. The caller must
33: reach the third step only after the input is confirmed sendable, must call
34: ``Reservation.sent()`` exactly once immediately before dispatch, and must
35: propagate ``BudgetExhausted`` as the deterministic rejection instead of
36: sending (never bypass it, never retry).
37: 
38: Semantics
39: ---------
40: - A successful ``reserve()`` immediately debits one slot (``remaining()``
41:   decreases, ``request_count`` increases).
42: - ``Reservation.sent()`` marks the slot as dispatched exactly once; it does not
43:   change the counters.
44: - ``Reservation.halt()`` refunds a slot that was reserved but never sent, at
45:   most once; it is a no-op after ``sent()``.
46: - A reservation never sent and never halted keeps its slot (fail-closed).
47: - A failed transport send does not refund the slot (no implicit retry).
48: - There is intentionally no way to reset, clear, refill, restore or renew a
49:   budget; remaining allowance is monotonically non-increasing.
50: 
51: When the module is not imported nothing changes: the upstream baseline
52: behaviour is preserved. When constructed with no configured limit (``None`` or
53: ``UNMETERED``) the budget is unmetered and never refuses a request.
54: 
55: Only the standard library (``threading``, ``typing``) is used: no network, no
56: SDK/provider client imports and no implicit retries live in this module.
57: """
58: 
59: from __future__ import annotations
60: 
61: import threading
62: from typing import Final
63: 
64: __all__ = [
65:     "UNMETERED",
66:     "BudgetExhausted",
67:     "RequestBudget",
68:     "Reservation",
69: ]
70: 
71: 
72: class _Unmetered:
73:     """Sentinel type for the unmetered budget mode (NFR-01)."""
74: 
75:     __slots__ = ()
76: 
77:     def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - diagnostics only
78:         return "UNMETERED"
79: 
80:     def __bool__(self) -> bool:  # pragma: no cover - diagnostics only
81:         # Never let a truthiness test silently turn the sentinel into a limit.
82:         return True
83: 
84: 
85: #: Module-level sentinel meaning "no configured limit" (NFR-01).
86: UNMETERED: Final = _Unmetered()
87: 
88: #: Accepted ``limit`` argument types.
89: LimitLike = int | _Unmetered | None
90: 
91: 
92: class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
93:     """Deterministic rejection when no reservation is available (NFR-01).
94: 
95:     Attributes
96:     ----------
97:     code: always ``"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"`` (runtime-policy-catalog NFR-01 row).
98:     granted: number of slots already granted at the moment of refusal.
99:     limit: the configured per-run limit.
100:     """
101: 
102:     code: str = "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"
103: 
104:     def __init__(self, message: str, granted: int, limit: int) -> None:
105:         super().__init__(message)
106:         self.code = "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"
107:         self.granted = granted
108:         self.limit = limit
109: 
110: 
111: class Reservation:
112:     """A single dispatch slot granted by :meth:`RequestBudget.reserve`.
113: 
114:     NFR-01 / INV-02: a reservation is consumed at most once (``sent()``) and,
115:     while unused, may be refunded at most once (``halt()``).
116:     """
117: 
118:     __slots__ = ("_budget", "_slot", "_limit", "_sent", "_halted", "_lock")
119: 
120:     def __init__(
121:         self,
122:         budget: RequestBudget,
123:         *,
124:         slot: int,
125:         limit: int | None,
126:     ) -> None:
127:         self._budget = budget
128:         self._slot = slot
129:         self._limit = limit
130:         self._sent = False
131:         self._halted = False
132:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
133: 
134:     @property
135:     def slot(self) -> int:
136:         """1-based index of the granted slot within the run (NFR-01)."""
137:         return self._slot
138: 
139:     @property
140:     def limit(self) -> int | None:
141:         """Configured limit of the owning budget, ``None`` when unmetered."""
142:         return self._limit
143: 
144:     @property
145:     def sent_already(self) -> bool:
146:         """Whether this reservation has already been marked sent (INV-02)."""
147:         return self._sent
148: 
149:     def sent(self) -> None:
150:         """Consume the reservation exactly once, right before dispatch.
151: 
152:         NFR-01 / INV-02: the slot was already debited by ``reserve()``; this
153:         call only records that it was used, so counters do not change. A
154:         second call, or a call after ``halt()``, raises ``RuntimeError`` and
155:         must never lead to a second transport send.
156:         """
157:         with self._lock:
158:             if self._sent:
159:                 raise RuntimeError("reservation already consumed: sent() is single-use")
160:             if self._halted:
161:                 raise RuntimeError("reservation was halted and cannot be sent")
162:             self._sent = True
163: 
164:     def halt(self) -> None:
165:         """Refund the slot if it was reserved but never sent (idempotent).
166: 
167:         NFR-01: refunds at most once. After ``sent()`` the slot stays spent
168:         (a provider failure consumes the slot; no implicit retries). A slot
169:         that is neither sent nor halted stays occupied (fail-closed).
170:         """
171:         with self._lock:
172:             if self._halted or self._sent:
173:                 return
174:             self._halted = True
175:             self._budget._refund()  # noqa: SLF001 - owner-internal refund
176: 
177: 
178: class RequestBudget:
179:     """Per-run atomic request budget (NFR-01 / INV-02).
180: 
181:     ``limit`` is either a positive ``int`` (metered mode) or ``None`` /
182:     ``UNMETERED`` (unmetered, baseline behaviour). ``0``, negative ints,
183:     ``bool`` (explicitly excluded although it subclasses ``int``), floats and
184:     strings raise ``ValueError``.
185:     """
186: 
187:     __slots__ = ("_limit", "_granted", "_lock")
188: 
189:     def __init__(self, limit: LimitLike = None) -> None:
190:         self._limit = _validate_limit(limit)
191:         self._granted = 0
192:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
193: 
194:     @property
195:     def limit(self) -> int | None:
196:         """Configured limit, ``None`` when unmetered (NFR-01)."""
197:         return self._limit
198: 
199:     @property
200:     def metered(self) -> bool:
201:         """``True`` when a positive limit is enforced (NFR-01)."""
202:         return self._limit is not None
203: 
204:     def remaining(self) -> int | None:
205:         """Remaining allowance; always ``None`` in unmetered mode (NFR-01)."""
206:         with self._lock:
207:             if self._limit is None:
208:                 return None
209:             return self._limit - self._granted
210: 
211:     @property
212:     def request_count(self) -> int:
213:         """Number of slots currently consumed/occupied (NFR-01)."""
214:         with self._lock:
215:             return self._granted
216: 
217:     @property
218:     def exhausted(self) -> bool:
219:         """``True`` only when metered and no slot remains (NFR-01 / INV-02)."""
220:         with self._lock:
221:             if self._limit is None:
222:                 return False
223:             return self._limit - self._granted == 0
224: 
225:     def reserve(self) -> Reservation:
226:         """Atomically check and debit one slot, returning a ``Reservation``.
227: 
228:         NFR-01 / INV-02: the check-and-debit happens under one lock so that
229:         concurrent racers can never exceed the limit. When no slot remains a
230:         ``BudgetExhausted`` is raised, nothing is debited and nothing may be
231:         sent. Unmetered budgets never refuse and just count requests.
232:         """
233:         with self._lock:
234:             if self._limit is None:
235:                 self._granted += 1
236:                 return Reservation(self, slot=self._granted, limit=None)
237:             if self._granted >= self._limit:
238:                 raise BudgetExhausted(
239:                     "request budget exhausted: "
240:                     f"{self._granted} of {self._limit} slots granted",
241:                     granted=self._granted,
242:                     limit=self._limit,
243:                 )
244:             self._granted += 1
245:             return Reservation(self, slot=self._granted, limit=self._limit)
246: 
247:     def _refund(self) -> None:
248:         """Return one unsent slot to the budget (internal, NFR-01).
249: 
250:         Called only by :meth:`Reservation.halt` after it locked that the slot
251:         was neither sent nor previously refunded.
252:         """
253:         with self._lock:
254:             if self._granted > 0:
255:                 self._granted -= 1
256: 
257: 
258: def _validate_limit(limit: LimitLike) -> int | None:
259:     """Normalise ``limit`` to a positive int or ``None`` (NFR-01).
260: 
261:     Rejects ``bool`` explicitly (``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``), then any
262:     non-``int`` type and non-positive values.
263:     """
264:     if limit is None or isinstance(limit, _Unmetered):
265:         return None
266:     if isinstance(limit, bool):
267:         raise ValueError(f"request budget limit must be a positive int, got bool: {limit!r}")
268:     if not isinstance(limit, int):
269:         raise ValueError(
270:             "request budget limit must be a positive int, None or UNMETERED, "
271:             f"got {type(limit).__name__}: {limit!r}"
272:         )
273:     if limit <= 0:
274:         raise ValueError(f"request budget limit must be positive, got {limit!r}")
275:     return limit
```

1: # D9 — OpenCode launch prompt
2: 
3: Read `AGENTS.md` first, then this prompt and the referenced D1–D4 documents in the order prescribed by `AGENTS.md`. Use the course permission configuration and the current approved requirement and architecture revisions. This is the common launch prompt for all five requirements. The human specifies the requirement IDs, working revision and task scope in the session. If any are missing or the documents conflict, ask for clarification and stop. A request to implement a feature is not approval to begin coding.
4: 
5: ## Gate 1 — Plan and stop (`course-plan`)
6: 
7: Work read-only. Produce an execution plan covering:
8: 
9: 1. **Traceability:** map every selected D1 acceptance criterion and applicable invariant to its D2 component and planned test. Identify any affected shared boundary.
10: 2. **Interface contracts:** specify inputs, outputs, error states and ownership of each decision. Explain how the design preserves deterministic publication and dispatch rules where applicable.
11: 3. **Scope:** list the exact files to read and change, which baseline code must remain intact, and any explicit exclusions. Identify dependencies on other requirements. Never request broader permissions as a shortcut.
12: 4. **Verification:** specify fixed inputs, expected outcomes and commands for normal cases, negative cases and regressions. Include at least one test that would fail if each affected invariant were bypassed. Say which tests require live services; keep them separate from offline acceptance.
13: 5. **Steps and rollback:** give the order for tests, implementation, integration and self-checks, plus a safe rollback approach.
14: 
15: End with **WAITING FOR PLAN AND TEST APPROVAL**. Do not generate or edit implementation or test code at this gate. The human reviewer records the approved plan, test criteria, exact paths, approver and time. A revision to scope, contracts, invariants or acceptance criteria requires a new plan and approval.
16: 
17: ## Gate 2 — Build only the approved change (`course-build`)
18: 
19: When the human switches to Build, require the approved plan and test reference; do not infer approval from a role switch. Have the human approve allowed edits against the exact reviewed paths. Write only the approved tests first. Ask the human to run them against the pre-change behavior and confirm that the key missing-behavior case fails for the expected reason. Stop for human confirmation of that result before editing production code.
20: 
21: Implement the smallest change that satisfies the approved plan. Respect module boundaries, keep the upstream baseline and existing tests intact, and leave governance, CI and permissions to the human. Do not weaken a test to pass or circumvent a rejected edit. If a new dependency, broader path, changed contract or test change is needed, explain it and stop for review.
22: 
23: Summarize the changes, unresolved risks and D4 checks the human should run. End with **WAITING FOR VERIFICATION EVIDENCE**. Do not use shell or external tools.
24: 
25: ## Gate 3 — Self-check and review (`course-verify`)
26: 
27: Work read-only. Inspect the diff or changed files supplied by the human and map each actual result to its planned check. Request human-run structural checks, earlier regression suites and the affected behavioral and invariant checks. Require normal positive controls and adverse cases; keep unavailable, skipped or unrun checks distinct from passes. For application prompt/model changes, request the agreed fixed semantic evaluation evidence before recommending approval.
28: 
29: Return a proposed review summary: requirement IDs, reviewed revision, tests and results, unmet criteria, risks and recommended verdict. Stop for human review. If evidence shows a defect, propose a repair and repeat the appropriate approval and verification gates. Only the human makes the final verdict and controls Git, publishing and merge.
30: 
31: Keep the actual session and mark human interruptions, redirects, approvals and rejections with their rationale. Give the human a summary for the review memo and AI-use log. Never invent evidence, and keep credentials, student identifiers and raw sessions out of the public repository.
32: 
33: ## Task header and handoff required before Gate 1
34: 
35: The human supplies: selected requirement/invariant IDs; common starting SHA and current feature HEAD; contract revision C0–C5; developer and human reviewer; exact read/edit paths; planned case IDs and fixture revision; Python/dependency and OpenCode versions; offline/live scope; and the place to retain private raw sessions. Missing information is an open item, never filled with a fictional approval.
36: 
37: Read the documentation index, open review items in `docs/review-memo.md`, and `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`. If required material is denied by the current allowlist, report the exact missing paths and stop for human maintenance. The registry status `proposed` is not Build approval. Freeze shared fields/signatures with affected owners first. Use mocks to develop independently, then require integrated evidence with the real components.
38: 
39: Before production edits, the human approves the exact test-design revision; implementation approval and final PR approval are distinct. An ImportError, dependency failure, absent module or no collected tests is not the required failing-before behavior evidence. Record such setup gaps separately and obtain an approved approach to test the baseline behavior. After any approved fixture/expectation change, record why and renew review rather than silently moving the target.
40: 
41: Only actual actions belong in the session record. Keep planning and document review distinct from OpenCode implementation sessions, and record the actual tool, scope and session reference in the AI-use log. Follow the course OpenCode implementation workflow. This launch prompt does not authorize another tool to bypass denied actions or turn advisory output into human approval.
42:

44: ## Applying interface v1.0

46: Use the named shared records and callable boundaries in C0–C5; do not reopen or invent different field meanings per feature. A task plan lists exact integration adapters and tests the specified compatibility views. Internal class choices may vary without changing shared records. Apply task-specific entry criteria from the review memo; independent offline work may use approved fixtures. A team's confirmation of this document is not automatic approval of every feature plan/test.

48: Use the approved product run-profile limit and verify outbound attempts at the transport boundary. Distinguish charged safety slots, known sends and unknown delivery in receipts. Diagnostic limits are separate from product acceptance; charged attempts do not establish billed model usage.

10: 
11: A provider failure after dispatch consumes the slot; no implicit retries are allowed in supported metered runs. Runtime diagnostic outputs must not masquerade as official recommendations.
12: 
13: ## Combined-path precedence (C0–C5)
14: 
15: 1. Validate/reduce scoped context before reserving a model slot. CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE means no send or budget debit for that rejected request.
16: 2. If context is ready but C4 has no slot, return BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Both terminal paths suppress any earlier candidate as an official final recommendation.
17: 3. Invalid financial records are excluded; optional sentiment failures preserve per-source reasons and UNKNOWN/null where appropriate. Continue usable analysis rather than treating absent sentiment as a neutral signal or unconditional publication failure.
18: 4. On nonzero source coverage but failed assessment, keep PARTIAL_DATA/AVAILABLE and record assessment failure with UNKNOWN/null. Coverage is collection state, not model confidence.
19: 5. Gate any resulting candidate at every official sink. A source placeholder is not substantive evidence. Publication passes only when C1 succeeds, regardless of a model's requested rating.
20: 
21: A user retry after a terminal failure is a new run with a new identity; do not resume the same metered identity with a fresh counter. Invalid configuration or unknown contract version blocks the affected task before live dispatch. Record implementation and case evidence for each failure path.
22: 
23: Each enforcing component emits the specified receipt fields. Verification records identify the producing path, implementation revision and observed result.

1: # ADR-001 — Deterministic extensions at existing application boundaries
2: 
3: Status: Proposed. Interface version: 1.0.
4: 
5: ## Context and drivers
6: 
7: The extension preserves the existing single-stock graph, model clients, data providers and publication paths. Architectural drivers are verifiable outputs, explicit degraded behavior, bounded dispatch, limited baseline changes and independent offline acceptance tests.
8: 
9: ## Decision process and alternatives
10: 
11: Trace the existing dispatch and publication paths, compare the candidates in the [evaluation table](../evaluation-table.md), define shared contracts and review adverse cases before implementation.
12: 
13: | Option | Assessment |
14: |---|---|
15: | Prompt and configuration changes only | Insufficient enforcement of publication, arithmetic, missing-data state and total request limits |
16: | Deterministic components at existing boundaries | Selected; supports the five acceptance contracts with localized integration |
17: | Replacement orchestration | Deferred; increases migration and regression scope without an identified requirement |
18: 
19: ## Component decisions
20: 
21: | Requirement | Decision |
22: |---|---|
23: | FR-01 | Resolve current-run evidence and apply one publication result at every official sink |
24: | FR-02 | Compute from validated operands; resolve immutable verified records by ID |
25: | FR-03 | Separate source coverage, assessment and execution state; 0/3 yields UNKNOWN/null without a sentiment-model call |
26: | NFR-01 | Atomically reserve capacity at a common outbound boundary |
27: | NFR-02 | Reduce optional history at the two scoped sites; reject irreducible messages before budget reservation |
28: 
29: Use [C0–C5](../interface-contracts.md) JSON-compatible shared records. Internal types may use adapters. Add separate owner keys to AgentState and retain legacy report strings as views of authoritative records.
30: 
31: ## Layered model context
32: 
33: Context layers are role/task identity, standing constraints, typed evidence and run state, active tool exchanges, optional discussion history and the current request. Mark required blocks explicitly.
34: 
35: Assembly order: prioritize and deduplicate optional history; measure the final representation; remove optional groups oldest first; reassemble; re-inject critical constraints; verify required blocks and tool pairs; recount before dispatch. Preserve authoritative stored evidence when reducing a request. Refuse a scoped request when mandatory content cannot fit.
36: 
37: NFR-02 uses a configurable 65536-byte message cap at analyst closure and the neutral risk role. It excludes separately bound tool schemas and is independent of token measurement.
38: 
39: ## Token-budget design
40: 
41: The input-token design uses a proposed cap of 16384 tokens and a compaction trigger above 13107 tokens (floor of 80% of the cap). Configure output allowance and provider-envelope reserve independently. Validate the selected model capacity, counting method, schema overhead and provider conversion before enabling this policy. Until then, token enforcement remains unverified. Byte counts are not a substitute for token counts.
42: 
43: ## Run profile
44: 
45: The initial product profile uses a configurable request limit of 40, both tiers on the school model alias, explicit thinking-disabled requests and an output allowance of 4096 tokens. NFR-01 boundary fixtures use limit 3. Configuration evidence accompanies baseline comparisons; changes to public semantics require a contract revision.
46: 
47: ## Consequences and review triggers
48: 
49: Benefits are localized changes and explicit failure states. Costs are shared dispatch/publication integration and nullable-state compatibility across existing consumers. Review this decision when provider retries become opaque, a sink bypasses publication checks, required context routinely cannot fit, or requirements need different orchestration.
50: 
51: Changes to shared fields, date semantics, thresholds, safety behavior or dependencies require affected-owner review and synchronized requirements, interfaces and tests. Record the human decision and supporting evidence.
```

1: # Memory and state design
2: 
3: | Requirement | Session state and lifecycle |
4: | --- | --- |
5: | FR-01 | Evidence/argument IDs and candidate status are scoped to one run; only allowed decisions reach existing decision memory. Do not resolve references from a prior run. |
6: | FR-02 | Verified records are immutable within a run; report may retain source references and immutable calculation records. No user-wide metric cache in first release. |
7: | FR-03 | Coverage and reasons are run-local; avoid persisting raw social responses. |
8: | NFR-01 | Counter is run-local; a resumed metered run must not reset spent slots. Disable upstream checkpoint resume for metered course runs until counters can be restored atomically; restart is a distinct run. |
9: | NFR-02 | Reduction is per request; optional context may be dropped from the sent payload only, not silently erased from approved evidence records. |
10: 
11: Reuse the upstream user-owned decision log for approved decisions only and retain its configured rotation/deletion behavior. Keep course fixtures isolated from users' local caches and memory. Reports may contain nonsecret source metadata; users control local retention. No credentials, raw model sessions or student identifiers belong in public logs. Repeatability claims require a new run or an explicitly versioned snapshot, not a retained LLM answer.
12: 
13: ## Shared state contract
14: 
15: Use C0 identity and C1–C3 authoritative records from [interface-contracts.md](interface-contracts.md). Add coverage/assessment state beside existing sentiment text; downstream readers use authoritative fields rather than reparsing a Neutral placeholder. Keep data coverage, assessment failure, execution completion and publication approval separate. New runs never inherit prior scores, references or counters.
16: 
17: Raw prompts, account details, personal API keys and complete vendor/social responses stay out of public logs and repository fixtures. Keep original private run receipts separately from shareable, synthetic test fixtures; record only approved references/hashes in public artifacts. Determine the team's actual retention duration before collecting new live payloads; no indefinite retention is implied.

28: The manual forbids treating a missing module, import error or uncollected
29: test as a valid counterexample. ``load_budget()`` therefore tries to import
30: the real owner module first. If it does not exist yet, it returns a minimal
31: ``BASELINE_STANDIN`` namespace that models the *unchanged upstream baseline*:

35: and fails as a clear assertion error before the implementation exists (for

66:     def __init__(self, fail: bool = False) -> None:
67:         self.send_count = 0

72:     def send(self, payload: str) -> None:
73:         # Count the attempt before raising so a failing send is observable.

97:     """Minimal standin for the unchanged upstream baseline.

99:     There is no counter, no limit and no rejection: every request is

103:     class Reservation:
104:         # Baseline reservations carry no slot identity whatsoever, so there is
105:         # nothing the tests can tell apart between two reservations.
106:         def sent(self) -> None:

108:             # this is a no-op (no counting, never raises).

110: 
111:         def halt(self) -> None:
112:             # Baseline has no slot to refund: aborting is a no-op as well.

119:             self.code = "BASELINE_NO_BUDGET"
120:             self.granted = -1

130:             # Baseline always allows the request: no counter, no refusal.
131:             self.sends += 1
132:             return Reservation()
133:

135:             # Baseline tracks no allowance at all.
136:             return None
137:

139:         def exhausted(self) -> bool:
140:             return False
141:

143:         def request_count(self) -> int:

436: # 8. INV-02: atomic reservation under concurrency

439: 
440: class _RaceOutcome:
441:     def __init__(self) -> None:
442:         self.granted = 0
443:         self.rejected = 0
444:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
445: 
446:     def record_granted(self) -> None:
447:         with self._lock:
448:             self.granted += 1
449: 
450:     def record_rejected(self) -> None:
451:         with self._lock:
452:             self.rejected += 1
453: 
454: 
455: def _race(budget, run, transport, threads: int) -> _RaceOutcome:
456:     """N threads reserve exactly one slot each after a shared barrier."""
457:     barrier = threading.Barrier(threads)
458:     outcome = _RaceOutcome()
459:     errors: list[BaseException] = []
460: 
461:     def worker(index: int) -> None:
462:         try:
463:             barrier.wait(timeout=10)
464:             reservation = run.reserve()
465:             reservation.sent()
466:             transport.send(f"race-{index}")
467:             outcome.record_granted()
468:         except budget.BudgetExhausted:
469:             outcome.record_rejected()
470:         except BaseException as exc:  # pragma: no cover - surfaced below
471:             errors.append(exc)
472: 
473:     workers = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(threads)]
474:     for thread in workers:
475:         thread.start()
476:     for thread in workers:
477:         thread.join(timeout=10)
478:     assert not errors, f"unexpected worker errors: {errors!r}"
479:     assert not any(thread.is_alive() for thread in workers), "worker deadlock"
480:     return outcome
481:

558: def test_exhausted_run_does_not_block_a_fresh_run(budget):
559:     """An exhausted run must not leak its state into a brand-new run.
560: 
561:     Two budget instances must never share a global counter: if they did, the
562:     first ``reserve()`` on ``run_b`` would be refused as soon as ``run_a`` had
563:     spent its three slots. ``run_b`` is created only *after* ``run_a`` is fully
564:     drained so the shared-counter defect is triggered on the very first call.
565:     """
566:     transport = FakeTransport()
567: 
568:     # Drain run_a completely through the shared reserve -> sent -> send order.
569:     run_a = budget.RequestBudget(LIMIT)
570:     for request in REQUESTS_EXACT:
571:         _reserve_one(run_a, transport, f"a-{request}")
572:     assert run_a.request_count == 3
573:     assert run_a.remaining() == 0
574: 
575:     # A fresh run created *after* run_a is exhausted must start full again.
576:     run_b = budget.RequestBudget(LIMIT)
577:     assert run_b is not run_a
578:     for request in REQUESTS_EXACT:
579:         _reserve_one(run_b, transport, f"b-{request}")
580: 
581:     assert transport.send_count == 6, "a shared counter would refuse run_b's sends"
582:     assert run_a.request_count == 3, "run_b's activity must not touch run_a"
583:     assert run_b.request_count == 3, "run_b must spend exactly its own limit"
584:     assert run_a.remaining() == 0
585:     assert run_b.remaining() == 0

588: def test_halt_after_sent_does_not_refund(budget):
589:     """A slot marked sent() must not be refundable, even after halt().

591:     This is the explicit negative counterpart of ``halt()`` refunding an
592:     unsent slot: once dispatched, ``halt()`` is a no-op (idempotent) and the
593:     remaining allowance stays exactly where ``sent()`` left it.
594:     """
595:     transport = FakeTransport()
596:     run = budget.RequestBudget(LIMIT)
597:     reservation = run.reserve()
598:     reservation.sent()

608: 
609:     assert run.remaining() == remaining_after_sent, "halt() must not refund a sent slot"
610:     assert run.request_count == 1, "a sent slot stays consumed"
611:     assert transport.send_count == 1, "halt() must not trigger any resend"
612: 
613:     # The remaining allowance is still enforced strictly. LIMIT == 3, and the
614:     # sent r1 slot is NOT refunded, so two of three slots are still spendable:
615:     # grant both, which leaves the run exactly exhausted — never LIMIT+1 total.
616:     reservation2 = run.reserve()
617:     reservation2.sent()
618:     transport.send("r2")
619:     assert run.remaining() == LIMIT - 2
620:     assert run.request_count == 2
621:     assert transport.send_count == 2
622: 
623:     reservation3 = run.reserve()
624:     reservation3.sent()
625:     transport.send("r3")
626:     assert run.remaining() == 0, "all three slots are consumed only if r1 was not refunded"
627:     assert run.request_count == 3
628:     assert transport.send_count == 3
629: 
630:     # Only now, with every slot spent, must the next reservation be refused.
631:     with pytest.raises(budget.BudgetExhausted):
632:         run.reserve()
633:     assert transport.send_count == 3, "the refunded-slot defect would allow a 4th send"

724: # 10. NFR-02 CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE rejection debits no budget
725: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

727: 
728: class _SpyBudget:
729:     """Counts reserve() calls to prove a rejection happened before reserve."""
730: 
731:     def __init__(self, inner_factory) -> None:
732:         self.inner = inner_factory()
733:         self.reserve_calls = 0
734: 
735:     def reserve(self):
736:         self.reserve_calls += 1
737:         return self.inner.reserve()
738: 
739: 
740: class _ContextTooLarge(ValueError):
741:     pass
742: 
743: 
744: def _prepare(mandatory_bytes: int, cap: int = 65536) -> None:
745:     """NFR-02 step 1/2: reduce, then confirm sendable. Never reserves."""
746:     if mandatory_bytes > cap:
747:         raise _ContextTooLarge("CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE")
748: 
749: 
750: def _scoped_send(run, transport, payload: str, mandatory_bytes: int) -> None:
751:     """Agreed order: confirm sendable -> reserve (once) -> send."""
752:     _prepare(mandatory_bytes)
753:     reservation = run.reserve()
754:     reservation.sent()
755:     transport.send(payload)
756: 
757: 
758: def test_context_too_large_is_rejected_before_any_reservation(budget):
759:     transport = FakeTransport()
760:     spy = _SpyBudget(lambda: budget.RequestBudget(LIMIT))
761: 
762:     with pytest.raises(_ContextTooLarge):
763:         _scoped_send(spy, transport, "oversize", mandatory_bytes=65537)
764: 
765:     assert spy.reserve_calls == 0, "rejection must precede reserve()"
766:     assert transport.send_count == 0
767:     assert spy.inner.remaining() == LIMIT, "a rejected request debits no budget"
768:     assert spy.inner.request_count == 0
769: 
770: 
771: def test_context_within_cap_reserves_exactly_once(budget):
772:     transport = FakeTransport()
773:     spy = _SpyBudget(lambda: budget.RequestBudget(LIMIT))
774: 
775:     _scoped_send(spy, transport, "fits", mandatory_bytes=65536)
776: 
777:     assert spy.reserve_calls == 1
778:     assert transport.send_count == 1
779:     assert spy.inner.remaining() == LIMIT - 1

Every fit criterion has a positive control; every invariant\n  has a negative test that fails if the enforcement is bypassed.\n\nFixture revision: nfr01-fixtures-v1 (inline, LIMIT = 3, run ids\n``run-A-0001`` / ``run-B-0002``). ``run_id`` and starts at zero); OPEN-3 settlement exclusion is a\nstatic source assertion (module source never imports or references\nsettlement); OPEN-4 sender exception -> ``ProviderFailure`` with ``dispatch()`` converts it into ``BudgetExhausted``\n(``\"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED\"``); OPEN-6 a second ``cancel_before_send`` is an\nidempotent no-op that releases headroom at most once, cancelling a object is imported at collection time\n  (``import ... as rb``); every other name is resolved inside the test body.\n  While the old draft API is still installed, collection succeeds and each\n  test fails at run time with an explicit traceability message.\n* All fixtures are inline: LIMIT = 3, a thread-safe FakeTransport that records\n  payloads/counts and can raise a synthetic OSError on a chosen call, and a\n  tiny PreparedRequest stub (status READY / CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE, messages).\n* Deterministic: no network, no sleeps, no clock dependence; concurrency uses\n  ``threading.Barrier`` \"run_id\",\n    \"limit\",\n    \"charged_attempts\",\n    \"known_sends\",\n    \"unknown_delivery\",\n    \"active_reservations\",\n    \"exhausted\",\n)\n\n\nclass PreparedRequest:\n    \"\"\"Tiny C5 PreparedRequest stub (v1 shared record layout).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, status: str = \"READY\", messages: list[dict] | None = None) -> None:\n        self.status = status\n        self.messages = [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"ping\"}] if messages is None else messages\n\n\nclass FakeTransport:\n    \"\"\"Thread-safe fake transport: records payloads and counts real sends.\n\n    ``send`` records the payload and increments ``send_count`` *before* the\n    optional synthetic OSError, so a failed attempt is still observable at the\n    transport boundary (C4: count actual fake sends, not the reported counter).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, fail_on_call: int | None = None) -> None:\n        self.payloads: list[object] = []\n        self.send_count = 0\n        self.attempts = 0\n        self._fail_on_call = fail_on_call\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def send(self, payload: object) -> str:\n        with self._lock:\n            self.attempts += 1\n            attempt = self.attempts\n            self.send_count += 1\n            self.payloads.append(payload)\n            fail_now = self._fail_on_call is not None and attempt  assert snap.charged_attempts == snap.known_sends + snap.unknown_delivery, (\n        \"C4 identity charged_attempts == known_sends + unknown_delivery \"\n        f\"violated: {fields}\"\n    )\n fields\n\n\ndef make_budget(run_id: str = RUN_A, limit: int = LIMIT):\n    return rb.RequestBudget(run_id=run_id, limit=limit)\n\n\ndef dispatch_ok(budget, transport: FakeTransport, prepared=None):\n    prepared = PreparedRequest() if prepared is None else prepared\n    return rb.dispatch(prepared, budget, transport.send)\n\n\ndef assert_no_official_rating(outcome, case_id: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A refusal must never surface a rating/Hold/default recommendation.\"\"\"\n    assert outcome is None, (\n        f\"{case_id}: a refused dispatch must not return a recommendation, got {outcome!r}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef assert_no_rating_in_exception(exc: BaseException, case_id: str) -> None:\n    text = repr(exc) + \" \" + str(exc)\n    for banned in (\"Hold\", \"Buy\", \"Sell\", \"rating\"):\n        assert banned.lower() not in text.lower(), (\n            f\"{case_id}: typed failure must not carry a {banned!r} decision: {text!r}\"\n        )\n"}

1: """Offline acceptance tests for C4 v1.0 - atomic per-run model dispatch.
2: 
3: Traceability
4: ------------
5: - Requirement NFR-01: a configurable shared limit on the *actual* model
6:   requests made within one stock-analysis main flow (docs/req/requirements.yaml).
7: - Invariant INV-02: requests in the metered analysis scope never exceed the
8:   run's configured call limit, including under concurrent dispatch
9:   (docs/architecture/invariants.md).
10: - Contract C4 - atomic per-run model dispatch
11:   (docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md, "C4" and the "V1 callable
12:   boundaries" table). Owner module:
13:   ``tradingagents/llm_clients/request_budget.py``. Planned calls:
14:   ``RequestBudget(run_id, limit)``, ``try_reserve()``, ``charge_attempt()``,
15:   ``cancel_before_send()``, ``snapshot()`` and
16:   ``dispatch(prepared, budget, send)``.
17: - ADR-001 (NFR-01 row): count dispatch at a common outbound boundary and
18:   atomically reserve a slot per run (docs/architecture/adr/001-choice-tbd.md).
19: - Runtime policy catalog NFR-01 / INV-02 and "Combined-path precedence":
20:   no slot -> BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no send, no official rating; a provider error
21:   after an attempted send consumes the slot; a C5 CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE rejection
22:   happens before reservation and debits no budget
23:   (docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md).
24: - verification-constraints.md: frozen case IDs T-NFR01-BOUNDARY,
25:   T-NFR01-RETRY, T-NFR01-ISOLATION, T-NFR01-FAILURE, T-NFR01-RESUME and
26:   T-INV02-RACE. Every fit criterion has a positive control; every invariant
27:   has a negative test that fails if the enforcement is bypassed.
28: 
29: Fixture revision: nfr01-fixtures-v1 (inline, LIMIT = 3, run ids
30: ``run-A-0001`` / ``run-B-0002``). Developer/owner: majiaqi-yan.
31: 
32: Approved interpretations (recorded in the Gate 1 plan, not re-opened here):
33: OPEN-2 resume disabled (no resume/restore/reset/refill API; a restarted run
34: uses a new ``run_id`` and starts at zero); OPEN-3 settlement exclusion is a
35: static source assertion (module source never imports or references
36: settlement); OPEN-4 sender exception -> ``ProviderFailure`` with code
37: ``"PROVIDER_FAILURE"`` and the original exception as ``__cause__``, slot stays
38: charged and ``unknown_delivery`` increments; OPEN-5 ``try_reserve()`` returns
39: ``None`` on refusal and ``dispatch()`` converts it into ``BudgetExhausted``
40: (``"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"``); OPEN-6 a second ``cancel_before_send`` is an

42: ticket raises ``RuntimeError``; OPEN-7 no UNMETERED/None/unlimited mode -
43: ``limit`` must be a positive ``int`` and ``bool`` is rejected.

45: Design notes

47: * Only the module object is imported at collection time

95: class FakeTransport:
96:     """Thread-safe fake transport: records payloads and counts real sends.
97: 
98:     ``send`` records the payload and increments ``send_count`` *before* the
99:     optional synthetic OSError, so a failed attempt is still observable at the
100:     transport boundary (C4: count actual fake sends, not the reported counter).
101:     """
102: 
103:     def __init__(self, fail_on_call: int | None = None) -> None:
104:         self.payloads: list[object] = []
105:         self.send_count = 0
106:         self.attempts = 0
107:         self._fail_on_call = fail_on_call
108:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
109: 
110:     def send(self, payload: object) -> str:
111:         with self._lock:
112:             self.attempts += 1
113:             attempt = self.attempts
114:             self.send_count += 1
115:             self.payloads.append(payload)
116:             fail_now = self._fail_on_call is not None and attempt == self._fail_on_call
117:         if fail_now:
118:             raise OSError("synthetic transport failure")
119:         return f"response-{attempt}"

No sleeps, no clock, no network; stdlib + pytest only.

## Contract ambiguities I had to interpret (not approved — please confirm)

1. **`ContextTooLarge` type location.** C4 says the failure types are "defined in the responsible owner module" and lists `ContextTooLarge`. My C5-first tests reference `rb.ContextTooLarge`, i.e. they assume `request_budget.py` re-exports or defines it. If NFR-02's `context_limit.py` owns the class instead, those two tests need an import change — a test edit, which requires your approval.
2. **Who calls `charge_attempt`, and the exact dispatch sequence.** C4's lifecycle (`try_reserve -> charge_attempt(ticket) -> send`) does not say whether `charge_attempt` marks the attempt before or after invoking `send`. My tests only assert observable outcomes (counts and transport calls), so both orderings pass; a provider failure must set `unknown_delivery` (OPEN-4), which I do assert.
3. **"increments `unknown_delivery`" (OPEN-4) vs. `known_sends`.** I read it as: a failed send counts in `unknown_delivery` and *not* in `known_sends`, hence `charged_attempts == known_sends + unknown_delivery` holds after one failure (1 == 0 + 1). If an implementation counts a failed send as also "known sent", that identity test will fail.
4. **Cancellation test naming.** `cancel_before_send` / double-cancel / cancel-after-charge have no dedicated frozen case ID; the spec attaches them to T-NFR01-FAILURE, so they carry the `test_t_nfr01_failure_...` prefix. Any reclassification is a test rename you'd need to approve.
5. **Reused `run_id` with a new instance.** Since resume is disabled (OPEN-2), I assert that constructing a second budget with the *same* `run_id` yields a fresh local counter (0), while the original instance stays exhausted. That is a design choice: the contract does not forbid two live objects sharing a `run_id`. If you want that rejected instead, it's a test change.
6. **`limit=None` rejection.** OPEN-7 says no unmetered mode, so I expect `ValueError` for `limit=None`. The old draft accepted `None` as "unmetered", so this is the deliberate inversion.

Note: `assert_no_rating_in_exception` checks that the exception text never contains "Hold"/"Buy"/"Sell"/"rating". That is a heuristic (a message like "no rating produced" would fail it); if that wording could appear, say so and I'll narrow the check.

python -m pytest -q test/offline/test_request_budget.py
```

and confirm each test fails at run time for the expected reason (missing C4 API) before I edit any production code.

- typed failures: BudgetExhausted, ContextTooLarge, ProviderFailure (each with a class attribute code: "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED", "CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE", "PROVIDER_FAILURE")

SEMANTICS:
1. Validation (raise ValueError for every invalid case, never TypeError): run_id must be a non-empty str (None, "", bool rejected); limit must be an int, not bool, > 0; a missing limit (default None) is invalid. Do not define an UNMETERED sentinel or any unlimited mode.
2. Accounting: counters are run-local. Under one lock: try_reserve() returns None when charged_attempts + active_reservations >= limit, otherwise creates a Reservation(reservation_id, run_id, state="reserved") and increments active_reservations. Reservation ids must be unique per budget instance.
3. charge_attempt(ticket): only a reservation of this budget in state "reserved" may be charged; it moves to "charged", decrements active_reservations, increments charged_attempts, and increments unknown_delivery (an attempt whose delivery is unconfirmed until proven).
4. On confirmed delivery the module must decrement unknown_delivery and increment known_sends, so that the identity charged_attempts == known_sends + unknown_delivery always holds. On an ambiguous provider error, unknown_delivery stays counted (no refund).
5. cancel_before_send(ticket): a "reserved" reservation moves to "cancelled" and decrements active_reservations; cancelling an already "cancelled" ticket is an idempotent no-op that releases headroom at most once; cancelling a "charged" ticket raises RuntimeError and never refunds.
6. snapshot() returns an immutable object exposing exactly these field names: run_id, limit, charged_attempts, known_sends, unknown_delivery, active_reservations, exhausted. exhausted means charged_attempts + active_reservations >= limit. Do not add a field named remaining and do not expose any mutable internal state.
7. dispatch(prepared, budget, send): read prepared.status; if it is not "READY", raise ContextTooLarge before reserving anything (C5-first: zero reservations, zero debits). Otherwise reserve one slot; on None raise BudgetExhausted; charge the attempt at the attempt boundary; invoke send exactly once with prepared.messages (fall back to prepared itself only if it has no messages attribute); on sender exception raise ProviderFailure with the original exception as __cause__ (the slot stays charged and the attempt stays in unknown_delivery); on success mark the attempt delivered and return the sender's response. Never return a placeholder decision, never synthesise a Hold/Buy/Sell/rating.
8. Concurrency: all state transitions and snapshot reads must be atomic under a threading.Lock; the last-slot race must produce exactly one reservation and one refusal. No sleeps, no busy-wait, no global mutable state.
9. No resume/restore/reset/refill/renew/release API at module or instance level: resume is disabled (a restarted run uses a new run_id and starts at zero). Do not import or reference any reconciliation/settlement module.

HARD TEXT CONSTRAINTS (tests enforce them):
- The module source must not contain the substring "settle" (case-insensitive) anywhere, including docstrings and comments. Describe exclusions as "historical reconciliation is out of scope" instead.
- No exception message, docstring or repr may contain the words hold, buy, sell or rating (case-insensitive, substring match). Avoid "threshold" because it contains "hold".
- Module docstring must state: Requirement NFR-01, Invariant INV-02, Contract C4, owner module and revision 486a9a5.

STYLE: module docstring, dataclasses with __slots__ or frozen dataclasses, explicit type hints, no prints, no logging side effects, English comments only where they explain a non-obvious invariant. Keep it as small as the contract allows (roughly 150-220 lines).

Do not edit any other file, do not edit tests, do not change configuration. Do not run shell commands; the human runs the verification.

When done, report: the final public API list, the state machine (reserved/charged/cancelled and counter transitions), how the two C4 identities are preserved, and anything in the contract you had to interpret.

103:     def __init__(self, fail_on_call: int | None = None) -> None:
104:         self.payloads: list[object] = []
105:         self.send_count = 0
106:         self.attempts = 0
107:         self._fail_on_call = fail_on_call
108:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
109: 
110:     def send(self, payload: object) -> str:
111:         with self._lock:
112:             self.attempts += 1
113:             attempt = self.attempts
114:             self.send_count += 1
115:             self.payloads.append(payload)

659: def test_t_inv02_race_two_contenders_last_slot_once():
660:     """T-INV02-RACE: INV-02/NFR-01/C4 - exactly one send and one refusal."""
661:     iterations = 20
662:     for iteration in range(iterations):
663:         budget = make_budget()
664:         transport = FakeTransport()
665:         # Spend LIMIT - 1 slots through real sends so the race is for the last one.
666:         for _ in range(LIMIT - 1):
667:             dispatch_ok(budget, transport)
668:         assert transport.send_count == LIMIT - 1
669: 
670:         barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
671:         granted: list[int] = []
672:         refused: list[int] = []
673:         errors: list[BaseException] = []
674: 
675:         def worker(index: int, budget=budget, transport=transport, barrier=barrier,
676:                    granted=granted, refused=refused, errors=errors):
677:             try:
678:                 barrier.wait(timeout=10)
679:                 ticket = budget.try_reserve()
680:                 if ticket is None:
681:                     refused.append(index)
682:                     return
683:                 budget.charge_attempt(ticket)
684:                 transport.send(f"race-{index}")
685:                 granted.append(index)
686:             except BaseException as exc:  # surfaced below
687:                 errors.append(exc)
688: 
689:         threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(2)]
690:         for thread in threads:
691:             thread.start()
692:         for thread in threads:
693:             thread.join(timeout=10)
694: 
695:         assert not errors, f"iteration {iteration}: worker errors {errors!r}"
696:         assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads), f"iteration {iteration}: deadlock"
697:         assert len(granted) == 1, f"iteration {iteration}: exactly one winner, got {granted}"
698:         assert len(refused) == 1, f"iteration {iteration}: exactly one refusal, got {refused}"
699:         assert transport.send_count == LIMIT, (
700:             f"iteration {iteration}: the last-slot race must cause exactly one extra send"
701:         )
702:         snap = snapshot_of(budget)
703:         assert snap["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
704:         assert snap["known_sends"] == LIMIT
705:         assert snap["exhausted"] is True

1: """Per-run model-request budget: one atomic reservation per dispatch.
2: 
3: Traceability
4: ------------
5: - Requirement NFR-01: a configurable shared limit on the actual model requests
6:   made within one stock-analysis main flow (docs/req/requirements.yaml).
7: - Invariant INV-02: requests in the metered analysis scope never exceed the
8:   run's configured call limit, including under concurrent dispatch
9:   (docs/architecture/invariants.md). Enforcer: "per-run atomic dispatch
10:   reservation"; verification: race two sends for the last slot and confirm the
11:   actual transport requests never exceed the cap; operational fallback: reject
12:   further dispatches and mark the run ``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`` with no official
13:   rating.
14: - ADR-001 (NFR-01 row): "count dispatch at a common transport boundary;
15:   atomically reserve a slot per run" (docs/architecture/adr/001-choice-tbd.md).
16: - Runtime policy catalog (docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md):
17:   * NFR-01 / INV-02, "no reservation available" -> abort the main analysis
18:     before send and deny publication; observable result ``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``
19:     and no official rating.
20:   * A provider failure after dispatch consumes the slot; no implicit retries
21:     are allowed in supported metered runs.
22:   * NFR-02 ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` is decided before reserving a slot and debits
23:     no budget for the rejected request.
24: 
25: Scope and shared entry ordering
26: -------------------------------
27: This module owns exactly one step of the shared metered entry::
28: 
29:     check / reduce input -> confirm sendable -> reserve one slot -> send
30: 
31: Context sizing/reduction (NFR-02) and publication gating (FR-01 / INV-01) are
32: owned elsewhere and are deliberately not implemented here. The caller must
33: reach the third step only after the input is confirmed sendable, must call
34: ``Reservation.sent()`` exactly once immediately before dispatch, and must
35: propagate ``BudgetExhausted`` as the deterministic rejection instead of
36: sending (never bypass it, never retry).
37: 
38: Semantics
39: ---------
40: - A successful ``reserve()`` immediately debits one slot (``remaining()``
41:   decreases, ``request_count`` increases).
42: - ``Reservation.sent()`` marks the slot as dispatched exactly once; it does not
43:   change the counters.
44: - ``Reservation.halt()`` refunds a slot that was reserved but never sent, at
45:   most once; it is a no-op after ``sent()``.
46: - A reservation never sent and never halted keeps its slot (fail-closed).
47: - A failed transport send does not refund the slot (no implicit retry).
48: - There is intentionally no way to reset, clear, refill, restore or renew a
49:   budget; remaining allowance is monotonically non-increasing.
50: 
51: When the module is not imported nothing changes: the upstream baseline
52: behaviour is preserved. When constructed with no configured limit (``None`` or
53: ``UNMETERED``) the budget is unmetered and never refuses a request.
54: 
55: Only the standard library (``threading``, ``typing``) is used: no network, no
56: SDK/provider client imports and no implicit retries live in this module.
57: """

59: from __future__ import annotations
60: 
61: import threading
62: from typing import Final
63: 
64: __all__ = [
65:     "UNMETERED",
66:     "BudgetExhausted",
67:     "RequestBudget",
68:     "Reservation",
69: ]

72: class _Unmetered:
73:     """Sentinel type for the unmetered budget mode (NFR-01)."""
74: 
75:     __slots__ = ()
76: 
77:     def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - diagnostics only
78:         return "UNMETERED"
79: 
80:     def __bool__(self) -> bool:  # pragma: no cover - diagnostics only
81:         # Never let a truthiness test silently turn the sentinel into a limit.
82:         return True
83: 
84: 
85: #: Module-level sentinel meaning "no configured limit" (NFR-01).
86: UNMETERED: Final = _Unmetered()
87: 
88: #: Accepted ``limit`` argument types.
89: LimitLike = int | _Unmetered | None

92: class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
93:     """Deterministic rejection when no reservation is available (NFR-01).
94: 
95:     Attributes
96:     ----------
97:     code: always ``"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"`` (runtime-policy-catalog NFR-01 row).
98:     granted: number of slots already granted at the moment of refusal.
99:     limit: the configured per-run limit.
100:     """
101: 
102:     code: str = "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"
103: 
104:     def __init__(self, message: str, granted: int, limit: int) -> None:
105:         super().__init__(message)
106:         self.code = "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"
107:         self.granted = granted
108:         self.limit = limit

111: class Reservation:
112:     """A single dispatch slot granted by :meth:`RequestBudget.reserve`.
113: 
114:     NFR-01 / INV-02: a reservation is consumed at most once (``sent()``) and,
115:     while unused, may be refunded at most once (``halt()``).
116:     """
117: 
118:     __slots__ = ("_budget", "_slot", "_limit", "_sent", "_halted", "_lock")
119: 
120:     def __init__(
121:         self,
122:         budget: RequestBudget,
123:         *,
124:         slot: int,
125:         limit: int | None,
126:     ) -> None:
127:         self._budget = budget
128:         self._slot = slot
129:         self._limit = limit
130:         self._sent = False
131:         self._halted = False
132:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
133: 
134:     @property
135:     def slot(self) -> int:
136:         """1-based index of the granted slot within the run (NFR-01)."""
137:         return self._slot
138: 
139:     @property
140:     def limit(self) -> int | None:
141:         """Configured limit of the owning budget, ``None`` when unmetered."""
142:         return self._limit
143: 
144:     @property
145:     def sent_already(self) -> bool:
146:         """Whether this reservation has already been marked sent (INV-02)."""
147:         return self._sent
148: 
149:     def sent(self) -> None:
150:         """Consume the reservation exactly once, right before dispatch.
151: 
152:         NFR-01 / INV-02: the slot was already debited by ``reserve()``; this
153:         call only records that it was used, so counters do not change. A
154:         second call, or a call after ``halt()``, raises ``RuntimeError`` and
155:         must never lead to a second transport send.
156:         """
157:         with self._lock:
158:             if self._sent:
159:                 raise RuntimeError("reservation already consumed: sent() is single-use")
160:             if self._halted:
161:                 raise RuntimeError("reservation was halted and cannot be sent")
162:             self._sent = True
163: 
164:     def halt(self) -> None:
165:         """Refund the slot if it was reserved but never sent (idempotent).
166: 
167:         NFR-01: refunds at most once. After ``sent()`` the slot stays spent
168:         (a provider failure consumes the slot; no implicit retries). A slot
169:         that is neither sent nor halted stays occupied (fail-closed).
170:         """
171:         with self._lock:
172:             if self._halted or self._sent:
173:                 return
174:             self._halted = True
175:             self._budget._refund()  # noqa: SLF001 - owner-internal refund
176: 
177: 
178: class RequestBudget:
179:     """Per-run atomic request budget (NFR-01 / INV-02).
180: 
181:     ``limit`` is either a positive ``int`` (metered mode) or ``None`` /
182:     ``UNMETERED`` (unmetered, baseline behaviour). ``0``, negative ints,
183:     ``bool`` (explicitly excluded although it subclasses ``int``), floats and
184:     strings raise ``ValueError``.
185:     """
186: 
187:     __slots__ = ("_limit", "_granted", "_lock")
188: 
189:     def __init__(self, limit: LimitLike = None) -> None:
190:         self._limit = _validate_limit(limit)
191:         self._granted = 0
192:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
193: 
194:     @property
195:     def limit(self) -> int | None:
196:         """Configured limit, ``None`` when unmetered (NFR-01)."""
197:         return self._limit
198: 
199:     @property
200:     def metered(self) -> bool:
201:         """``True`` when a positive limit is enforced (NFR-01)."""
202:         return self._limit is not None
203: 
204:     def remaining(self) -> int | None:
205:         """Remaining allowance; always ``None`` in unmetered mode (NFR-01)."""
206:         with self._lock:
207:             if self._limit is None:
208:                 return None
209:             return self._limit - self._granted
210: 
211:     @property
212:     def request_count(self) -> int:
213:         """Number of slots currently consumed/occupied (NFR-01)."""
214:         with self._lock:
215:             return self._granted
216: 
217:     @property
218:     def exhausted(self) -> bool:
219:         """``True`` only when metered and no slot remains (NFR-01 / INV-02)."""
220:         with self._lock:
221:             if self._limit is None:
222:                 return False
223:             return self._limit - self._granted == 0
224: 
225:     def reserve(self) -> Reservation:
226:         """Atomically check and debit one slot, returning a ``Reservation``.
227: 
228:         NFR-01 / INV-02: the check-and-debit happens under one lock so that
229:         concurrent racers can never exceed the limit. When no slot remains a
230:         ``BudgetExhausted`` is raised, nothing is debited and nothing may be
231:         sent. Unmetered budgets never refuse and just count requests.
232:         """
233:         with self._lock:
234:             if self._limit is None:
235:                 self._granted += 1
236:                 return Reservation(self, slot=self._granted, limit=None)
237:             if self._granted >= self._limit:
238:                 raise BudgetExhausted(
239:                     "request budget exhausted: "
240:                     f"{self._granted} of {self._limit} slots granted",
241:                     granted=self._granted,
242:                     limit=self._limit,
243:                 )
244:             self._granted += 1
245:             return Reservation(self, slot=self._granted, limit=self._limit)
246: 
247:     def _refund(self) -> None:
248:         """Return one unsent slot to the budget (internal, NFR-01).
249: 
250:         Called only by :meth:`Reservation.halt` after it locked that the slot
251:         was neither sent nor previously refunded.
252:         """
253:         with self._lock:
254:             if self._granted > 0:
255:                 self._granted -= 1
256: 
257: 
258: def _validate_limit(limit: LimitLike) -> int | None:
259:     """Normalise ``limit`` to a positive int or ``None`` (NFR-01).
260: 
261:     Rejects ``bool`` explicitly (``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``), then any
262:     non-``int`` type and non-positive values.
263:     """
264:     if limit is None or isinstance(limit, _Unmetered):
265:         return None
266:     if isinstance(limit, bool):
267:         raise ValueError(f"request budget limit must be a positive int, got bool: {limit!r}")
268:     if not isinstance(limit, int):
269:         raise ValueError(
270:             "request budget limit must be a positive int, None or UNMETERED, "
271:             f"got {type(limit).__name__}: {limit!r}"
272:         )
273:     if limit <= 0:
274:         raise ValueError(f"request budget limit must be positive, got {limit!r}")
275:     return limit
