10: | NFR-01 / INV-02 | Request budget owns the atomic run counter. Only a reserved dispatch may send. |
11: | NFR-02 | Context limit owns payload sizing and deterministic reduction; it cannot bypass the budget or remove mandatory content. |
12: 
13: For each new or modified module and function, document the associated requirement, ADR and invariant where applicable in a short comment or docstring. Preserve stable baseline behavior outside approved scope; do not add providers, packages or cross-layer imports without architecture review.

6: def normalize_content(response):
7:     """Normalize LLM response content to a plain string.
8: 
9:     Multiple providers (OpenAI Responses API, Google Gemini 3) return content
10:     as a list of typed blocks, e.g. [{'type': 'reasoning', ...}, {'type': 'text', 'text': '...'}].
11:     Downstream agents expect response.content to be a string. This extracts
12:     and joins the text blocks, discarding reasoning/metadata blocks.

15:     if isinstance(content, list):
16:         texts = [
17:             item.get("text", "") if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text"
18:             else item if isinstance(item, str) else ""
19:             for item in content
20:         ]
21:         response.content = "\n".join(t for t in texts if t)
22:     return response

96:     kwargs = {}

41: def _coerce(value: str, reference):
42:     """Coerce env-var string to the type of the existing default value.

52:         if normalized in _BOOL_FALSE:

54:         raise ValueError(

56:         )
57:     if isinstance(reference, int) and not isinstance(reference, bool):
58:         return int(value)
59:     if isinstance(reference, float):
60:         return float(value)
61:     return value

167:     def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
168:         """Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.
169: 
170:         ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the
171:         crypto pipeline (``"crypto"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects
172:         from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When
173:         ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with
174:         a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last
175:         successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.
176: 
177:         Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier
178:         ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``"REVIEW"``
179:         when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with
180:         ``tradingagents.agents.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the
181:         PortfolioRating enum.
182:         """
183:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)
184: 
185:         with run_config(self.config), \
186:                 self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio) as thread_id_value:
187:             return self._run_graph(
188:                 company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,
189:                 checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value, portfolio=portfolio,
190:             )
191: 
192:     def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None) -> str | None:
193:         """Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the
194:         ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``
195:         when checkpointing is disabled).
196: 
197:         Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``. Both
198:         ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use
199:         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup
200:         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less
201:         graph, making the flag a no-op.
202:         """
203:         self._resuming = False
204:         if not self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
205:             return None
206:         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)
207:         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name)
208:         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()
209:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)
210: 
211:         step = checkpoint_step(
212:             self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature
213:         )
214:         self._resuming = step is not None
215:         if step is not None:
216:             logger.info("Resuming from step %d for %s on %s", step, company_name, trade_date)
217:         else:
218:             logger.info("Starting fresh for %s on %s", company_name, trade_date)
219:         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)
220: 
221:     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):
222:         """The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,
223:         else the initial state for a fresh run.
224: 
225:         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;
226:         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message
227:         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).
228:         """
229:         return None if self._resuming else init_state
230: 
231:     def end_checkpoint(self):
232:         """Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run."""
233:         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:
234:             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
235:             self._checkpointer_ctx = None
236:             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()
237:         self._resuming = False
238: 
239:     @contextmanager
240:     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
241:         """Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path."""
242:         try:
243:             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
244:         finally:
245:             self.end_checkpoint()
246: 
247:     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
248:         """Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249)."""
249:         if self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
250:             clear_checkpoint(
251:                 self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date),
252:                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),
253:             )

255:     def run_settings(self) -> dict:
256:         """What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.
257: 
258:         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and
259:         local paths are never recorded.
260:         """
261:         cfg = self.config
262:         return {
263:             "version": tradingagents.__version__,
264:             "llm_provider": cfg.get("llm_provider"),
265:             "deep_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "deep") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
266:             "deep_think_llm": cfg.get("deep_think_llm"),
267:             "quick_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "quick") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
268:             "quick_think_llm": cfg.get("quick_think_llm"),
269:             "analysts": list(self.selected_analysts),
270:             "max_debate_rounds": cfg.get("max_debate_rounds"),
271:             "max_risk_discuss_rounds": cfg.get("max_risk_discuss_rounds"),
272:             "output_language": cfg.get("output_language"),
273:             "data_vendors": dict(cfg.get("data_vendors") or {}),
274:             "tool_vendors": dict(cfg.get("tool_vendors") or {}),
275:         }
276: 
277:     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:
278:         """Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.
279: 
280:         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass
281:         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the
282:         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.
283:         """
284:         if save_path is None:
285:             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)
286:         return write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html)
287: 
288:     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:
289:         """Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now."""
290:         stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
291:         return Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / "reports" / f"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}"
292: 
293:     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
294:         """Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.
295: 
296:         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The
297:         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles
298:         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).
299:         """
300:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)
301:         return self.propagator.create_initial_state(
302:             company_name,
303:             trade_date,
304:             asset_type=asset_type,
305:             instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),
306:             portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else "",
307:         )
308: 
309:     def _memory_step(self, state):
310:         """The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every
311:         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the
312:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).
313: 
314:         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,
315:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here
316:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in
317:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.
318:         """
319:         note = ""
320:         try:
321:             # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.
322:             done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)
323:             if done.failed:
324:                 note = (f"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run "
325:                         "and stay pending.")
326:         except Exception as exc:
327:             logger.warning("Settling past decisions failed: %s", exc)
328:             note = f"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending."
329:         try:
330:             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(
331:                 state["company_of_interest"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state["trade_date"]))
332:         except Exception as exc:
333:             logger.warning("Reading the memory log failed: %s", exc)
334:             past_context = ""
335:             note = note or f"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__})."
336:         return {"past_context": past_context, "memory_note": note}
337: 
338:     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:
339:         """Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.
340: 
341:         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own
342:         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done
343:         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to
344:         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.
345:         """
346:         with run_config(self.config):
347:             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)
348: 
349:     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:
350:         """Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).
351: 
352:         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would
353:         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.
354:         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.
355:         """
356:         with run_config(self.config):
357:             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)
358: 
359:     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):
360:         """Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log
361:         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here."""
362:         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)
363:         decision = final_state.get("final_trade_decision")
364:         if not decision:
365:             logger.warning("No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log",
366:                            company_name, trade_date)
367:             return
368:         self.memory_log.store_decision(
369:             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,
370:             rating=run_rating(final_state),
371:         )
372: 
373:     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock",
374:                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):
375:         """Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log."""
376:         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
377:         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()
378: 
379:         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same
380:         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).
381:         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:
382:             args.setdefault("config", {}).setdefault("configurable", {})["thread_id"] = checkpoint_thread_id
383: 
384:         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).
385:         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)
386:         if self.debug:
387:             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).
388:             final_state, printed = {}, set()
389:             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):
390:                 for msg in messages:
391:                     key = getattr(msg, "id", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, "content", None))
392:                     if key not in printed:
393:                         printed.add(key)
394:                         msg.pretty_print()
395:                 if state is not None:
396:                     final_state.update(state)
397:         else:
398:             final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)
399: 
400:         self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)
401: 
402:         # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.
403:         self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
404: 
405:         return final_state, run_rating(final_state)
406: 
407:     def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):
408:         """Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.
409: 
410:         ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``
411:         is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's
412:         graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.
413: 
414:         Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the
415:         analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages
416:         and reports come from their own finished steps ("tasks") as they happen.
417:         """
418:         args = {**args, "stream_mode": ["values", "tasks"]}
419:         # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even
420:         # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the
421:         # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.
422:         context = run_config_context(self.config)
423:         stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)
424:         try:
425:             while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:
426:                 namespace, mode, chunk = step
427:                 if namespace:
428:                     result = chunk.get("result") if mode == "tasks" else None
429:                     if isinstance(result, dict):
430:                         report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "messages" and v}
431:                         if result.get("messages") or report:
432:                             yield result.get("messages", []), report or None
433:                 elif mode == "values":
434:                     yield chunk.get("messages", []), chunk
435:         finally:
436:             context.run(stream.close)
437: 
438:     def _log_state(self, trade_date, final_state):

440:         entry = {
441:             "company_of_interest": final_state["company_of_interest"],
442:             "trade_date": final_state["trade_date"],
443:             "market_report": final_state["market_report"],
444:             "sentiment_report": final_state["sentiment_report"],
445:             "news_report": final_state["news_report"],
446:             "fundamentals_report": final_state["fundamentals_report"],
447:             "investment_debate_state": {
448:                 "bull_history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["bull_history"],
449:                 "bear_history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["bear_history"],
450:                 "history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["history"],
451:                 "current_response": final_state["investment_debate_state"][
452:                     "current_response"
453:                 ],
454:             },
455:             "trader_investment_plan": final_state["trader_investment_plan"],
456:             "risk_debate_state": {
457:                 "aggressive_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["aggressive_history"],
458:                 "conservative_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["conservative_history"],
459:                 "neutral_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["neutral_history"],
460:                 "history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["history"],
461:             },
462:             "investment_plan": final_state["investment_plan"],
463:             "final_trade_decision": final_state["final_trade_decision"],
464:             "final_rating": run_rating(final_state),
465:             "run_settings": self.run_settings(),
466:         }
467: 
468:         # A ticker that would escape the results directory is rejected.
469:         safe_ticker = safe_ticker_component(final_state["company_of_interest"])
470:         directory = Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / safe_ticker / "TradingAgentsStrategy_logs"
471:         directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
472: 
473:         log_path = directory / f"full_states_log_{trade_date}.json"
474:         with open(log_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
475:             # Reports can be in any language and this file is read by a person.
476:             json.dump(entry, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False)

### 2.4 Owner-module contract (`tradingagents/llm_clients/request_budget.py`)

```python
UNMETERED = <module sentinel object>          # "no limit configured" — baseline default

class RequestBudget:
    def __init__(self, limit: int | None): ...
    # limit: positive int, or None/UNMETERED → unmetered (no deny ever)
    # raises ValueError on 0, negative, bool, float, non-int-string

    def reserve(self) -> Reservation             # atomic under threading.Lock
    # grants  -> Reservation(slot=int, limit=int|None)
    # denies  -> raises BudgetExhausted(granted:int, limit:int)

    def remaining(self) -> int | None            # None when unmetered
    @property
    def exhausted(self) -> bool
    # request_count -> number of consumed slots (int|None)

class Reservation:
    def sent(self) -> None      # consumes the slot; second call raises RuntimeError
    def halt(self) -> None      # releases an unused slot back; idempotent
    limit: int | None

class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
    code = "BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"   # string constant, no enum (stdlib only)
    granted: int
    limit: int
```

**Shared entry order (agreed with NFR-02, unchanged):** *check/reduce input → confirm sendable → debit one slot → send.* This module owns exactly **step 3** and nothing else: `context_limit` MUST run its `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` rejection **before** `reserve()`, so a context rejection never debits (`RequestBudget` has no hook that lets it be called after a context check).

**Deterministic publication/dispatch preserved:** the budget has no opinion on ratings or publication; it only refuses dispatch. Refusal is a typed exception with a fixed `code`, so the integration seam can map it to `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` deterministically without model text.

**Failure handling:** unmetered → never denies (baseline). Metered deny → `BudgetExhausted`, never a warning-and-send. Send raising after `sent()` → slot stays consumed (catalog rule). Reservation abandoned without `sent()`/`halt()` → slot remains held for that run (fail-closed, never over-sends).

**Dependencies:** `threading`, `typing` only — no new package.

18:   atomically reserve a slot per run (docs/architecture/adr/001-choice-tbd.md).

20:   no slot -> BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no send, no official rating; a provider error
21:   after an attempted send consumes the slot; a C5 CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE rejection
22:   happens before reservation and debits no budget
23:   (docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md).
24: - verification-constraints.md: frozen case IDs T-NFR01-BOUNDARY,
25:   T-NFR01-RETRY, T-NFR01-ISOLATION, T-NFR01-FAILURE, T-NFR01-RESUME and
26:   T-INV02-RACE. Every fit criterion has a positive control; every invariant
27:   has a negative test that fails if the enforcement is bypassed.
28: 
29: Fixture revision: nfr01-fixtures-v1 (inline, LIMIT = 3, run ids
30: ``run-A-0001`` / ``run-B-0002``). Developer/owner: majiaqi-yan.
31: 
32: Approved interpretations (recorded in the Gate 1 plan, not re-opened here):
33: OPEN-2 resume disabled (no resume/restore/reset/refill API; a restarted run
34: uses a new ``run_id`` and starts at zero); OPEN-3 settlement exclusion is a
35: static source assertion (module source never imports or references
36: settlement); OPEN-4 sender exception -> ``ProviderFailure`` with code
37: ``"PROVIDER_FAILURE"`` and the original exception as ``__cause__``, slot stays
38: charged and ``unknown_delivery`` increments; OPEN-5 ``try_reserve()`` returns
39: ``None`` on refusal and ``dispatch()`` converts it into ``BudgetExhausted``
40: (``"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"``); OPEN-6 a second ``cancel_before_send`` is an
41: idempotent no-op that releases headroom at most once, cancelling a charged
42: ticket raises ``RuntimeError``; OPEN-7 no UNMETERED/None/unlimited mode -
43: ``limit`` must be a positive ``int`` and ``bool`` is rejected.
44: 
45: Design notes
46: ------------
47: * Only the module object is imported at collection time
48:   (``import ... as rb``); every other name is resolved inside the test body.
49:   While the old draft API is still installed, collection succeeds and each
50:   test fails at run time with an explicit traceability message.
51: * All fixtures are inline: LIMIT = 3, a thread-safe FakeTransport that records
52:   payloads/counts and can raise a synthetic OSError on a chosen call, and a
53:   tiny PreparedRequest stub (status READY / CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE, messages).
54: * Deterministic: no network, no sleeps, no clock dependence; concurrency uses
55:   ``threading.Barrier`` only.
56: * Standard library and pytest only.
57: """
58: 
59: from __future__ import annotations
60: 
61: import threading
62: 
63: import pytest
64: 
65: import tradingagents.llm_clients.request_budget as rb
66: 
67: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: # Inline fixtures - nfr01-fixtures-v1
69: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70: 
71: LIMIT = 3
72: RUN_A = "run-A-0001"
73: RUN_B = "run-B-0002"
74: MODULE_SOURCE = rb.__file__
75: 
76: SNAPSHOT_FIELDS = (
77:     "run_id",
78:     "limit",
79:     "charged_attempts",
80:     "known_sends",
81:     "unknown_delivery",
82:     "active_reservations",
83:     "exhausted",
84: )
85: 
86: 
87: class PreparedRequest:
88:     """Tiny C5 PreparedRequest stub (v1 shared record layout)."""
89: 
90:     def __init__(self, status: str = "READY", messages: list[dict] | None = None) -> None:
91:         self.status = status
92:         self.messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "ping"}] if messages is None else messages
93: 
94: 
95: class FakeTransport:
96:     """Thread-safe fake transport: records payloads and counts real sends.
97: 
98:     ``send`` records the payload and increments ``send_count`` *before* the
99:     optional synthetic OSError, so a failed attempt is still observable at the
100:     transport boundary (C4: count actual fake sends, not the reported counter).
101:     """
102: 
103:     def __init__(self, fail_on_call: int | None = None) -> None:
104:         self.payloads: list[object] = []
105:         self.send_count = 0
106:         self.attempts = 0
107:         self._fail_on_call = fail_on_call
108:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
109: 
110:     def send(self, payload: object) -> str:
111:         with self._lock:
112:             self.attempts += 1
113:             attempt = self.attempts
114:             self.send_count += 1
115:             self.payloads.append(payload)
116:             fail_now = self._fail_on_call is not None and attempt == self._fail_on_call
117:         if fail_now:
118:             raise OSError("synthetic transport failure")
119:         return f"response-{attempt}"
120: 
121: 
122: def snapshot_of(budget) -> dict:
123:     """Read and validate the C4 snapshot shape (exact field names)."""
124:     snap = budget.snapshot()
125:     fields = {name: getattr(snap, name, None) for name in SNAPSHOT_FIELDS}
126:     missing = [name for name in SNAPSHOT_FIELDS if not hasattr(snap, name)]
127:     assert not missing, (
128:         f"T-NFR01-BOUNDARY/C4: snapshot() must expose {missing}; "
129:         f"got attributes {sorted(dir(snap))}"
130:     )
131:     assert snap.charged_attempts == snap.known_sends + snap.unknown_delivery, (
132:         "C4 identity charged_attempts == known_sends + unknown_delivery "
133:         f"violated: {fields}"
134:     )
135:     assert snap.charged_attempts + snap.active_reservations <= snap.limit, (
136:         "C4 identity charged_attempts + active_reservations <= limit "
137:         f"violated: {fields}"
138:     )
139:     return fields
140: 
141: 
142: def make_budget(run_id: str = RUN_A, limit: int = LIMIT):
143:     return rb.RequestBudget(run_id=run_id, limit=limit)
144: 
145: 
146: def dispatch_ok(budget, transport: FakeTransport, prepared=None):
147:     prepared = PreparedRequest() if prepared is None else prepared
148:     return rb.dispatch(prepared, budget, transport.send)
149: 
150: 
151: def assert_no_official_rating(outcome, case_id: str) -> None:
152:     """A refusal must never surface a rating/Hold/default recommendation."""
153:     assert outcome is None, (
154:         f"{case_id}: a refused dispatch must not return a recommendation, got {outcome!r}"
155:     )
156: 
157: 
158: def assert_no_rating_in_exception(exc: BaseException, case_id: str) -> None:
159:     text = repr(exc) + " " + str(exc)
160:     for banned in ("Hold", "Buy", "Sell", "rating"):
161:         assert banned.lower() not in text.lower(), (
162:             f"{case_id}: typed failure must not carry a {banned!r} decision: {text!r}"
163:         )
164:

180:     snap = snapshot_of(budget)

182:     assert snap["limit"] == LIMIT
183:     assert snap["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
184:     assert snap["known_sends"] == LIMIT

358: def test_t_nfr01_isolation_two_runs_have_independent_counters():
359:     """T-NFR01-ISOLATION: NFR-01/C4 - counters are run-local."""

361:     transport = FakeTransport()
362:     dispatch_ok(run_a, transport)
363:     dispatch_ok(run_a, transport)
364:     dispatch_ok(run_b, transport)
365: 
366:     snap_a = snapshot_of(run_a)
367:     snap_b = snapshot_of(run_b)
368:     assert snap_a["run_id"] == RUN_A and snap_b["run_id"] == RUN_B
369:     assert snap_a["charged_attempts"] == 2
370:     assert snap_b["charged_attempts"] == 1

373: def test_t_nfr01_isolation_exhausted_run_does_not_block_fresh_run():
374:     """T-NFR01-ISOLATION: INV-02 - an exhausted run never blocks a new run."""
375:     transport = FakeTransport()
376:     run_a = make_budget(RUN_A)
377:     for _ in range(LIMIT):
378:         dispatch_ok(run_a, transport)
379:     assert snapshot_of(run_a)["exhausted"] is True
380: 
381:     run_b = make_budget(RUN_B)
382:     for _ in range(LIMIT):
383:         dispatch_ok(run_b, transport)
384:     assert transport.send_count == 2 * LIMIT
385:     assert snapshot_of(run_b)["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
386:     assert snapshot_of(run_a)["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
387:

389: def test_t_nfr01_isolation_concurrent_runs_are_thread_safe():
390:     """T-NFR01-ISOLATION: INV-02 - two threads, one per run, never share slots."""
391:     transport = FakeTransport()
392:     barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
393:     errors: list[BaseException] = []
394: 
395:     def worker(run):
396:         try:
397:             barrier.wait(timeout=10)
398:             for _ in range(LIMIT):
399:                 dispatch_ok(run, transport)
400:             with pytest.raises(rb.BudgetExhausted):
401:                 dispatch_ok(run, transport)
402:         except BaseException as exc:  # surfaced below
403:             errors.append(exc)
404: 
405:     run_a, run_b = make_budget(RUN_A), make_budget(RUN_B)
406:     threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(r,)) for r in (run_a, run_b)]
407:     for thread in threads:
408:         thread.start()
409:     for thread in threads:
410:         thread.join(timeout=10)
411: 
412:     assert not errors, f"unexpected worker errors: {errors!r}"
413:     assert transport.send_count == 2 * LIMIT
414:     assert snapshot_of(run_a)["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
415:     assert snapshot_of(run_b)["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
416:

418: def test_t_nfr01_isolation_reservation_occupies_headroom():
419:     """T-NFR01-ISOLATION: C4 - charged + active reservations never exceed limit."""
420:     budget = make_budget()
421:     transport = FakeTransport()
422:     ticket = budget.try_reserve()
423:     assert ticket is not None, "first reservation must succeed under limit 3"
424:     snap = snapshot_of(budget)
425:     assert snap["active_reservations"] == 1
426:     assert snap["charged_attempts"] == 0
427: 
428:     # Two more dispatches fill the remaining two slots; the reservation still
429:     # holds the third, so charged(2) + reserved(1) == limit and a further
430:     # dispatch is refused even though only two sends have happened.
431:     dispatch_ok(budget, transport)
432:     dispatch_ok(budget, transport)
433:     assert transport.send_count == 2
434:     with pytest.raises(rb.BudgetExhausted):
435:         dispatch_ok(budget, transport)
436:     assert transport.send_count == 2, "the held reservation must block a third send"
437:     snap = snapshot_of(budget)
438:     assert snap["active_reservations"] == 1
439:     assert snap["charged_attempts"] + snap["active_reservations"] == LIMIT
440:

540: def test_t_nfr01_resume_same_run_id_never_restores_spent_count():
541:     """T-NFR01-RESUME: INV-02 - re-using a run_id does not resume its counter."""
542:     # Two separate instances: there is no shared store, so the same run_id
543:     # gets a fresh local counter (resume disabled). The invariant we test is

659: def test_t_inv02_race_two_contenders_last_slot_once():
660:     """T-INV02-RACE: INV-02/NFR-01/C4 - exactly one send and one refusal."""
661:     iterations = 20
662:     for iteration in range(iterations):
663:         budget = make_budget()
664:         transport = FakeTransport()
665:         # Spend LIMIT - 1 slots through real sends so the race is for the last one.
666:         for _ in range(LIMIT - 1):
667:             dispatch_ok(budget, transport)
668:         assert transport.send_count == LIMIT - 1
669: 
670:         barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
671:         granted: list[int] = []
672:         refused: list[int] = []
673:         errors: list[BaseException] = []
674: 
675:         def worker(index: int, budget=budget, transport=transport, barrier=barrier,
676:                    granted=granted, refused=refused, errors=errors):
677:             try:
678:                 barrier.wait(timeout=10)
679:                 ticket = budget.try_reserve()
680:                 if ticket is None:
681:                     refused.append(index)
682:                     return
683:                 budget.charge_attempt(ticket)
684:                 transport.send(f"race-{index}")
685:                 granted.append(index)
686:             except BaseException as exc:  # surfaced below
687:                 errors.append(exc)
688: 
689:         threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(2)]
690:         for thread in threads:
691:             thread.start()
692:         for thread in threads:
693:             thread.join(timeout=10)
694: 
695:         assert not errors, f"iteration {iteration}: worker errors {errors!r}"
696:         assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads), f"iteration {iteration}: deadlock"
697:         assert len(granted) == 1, f"iteration {iteration}: exactly one winner, got {granted}"
698:         assert len(refused) == 1, f"iteration {iteration}: exactly one refusal, got {refused}"
699:         assert transport.send_count == LIMIT, (
700:             f"iteration {iteration}: the last-slot race must cause exactly one extra send"
701:         )
702:         snap = snapshot_of(budget)
703:         assert snap["charged_attempts"] == LIMIT
704:         assert snap["known_sends"] == LIMIT
705:         assert snap["exhausted"] is True
706:
